63:    * @brief Instance-based do-calculus utilities bound to a single CausalModel.
64:    *
65:    * This class provides:
66:    *  - AST builders for standard adjustment formulas:
67:    *      * Backdoor:  \f$\sum_{Z} P(y \mid x, z)\,P(z)\f$
68:    *      * Frontdoor: \f$\sum_{Z} P(z \mid x)\,\sum_{x} P(y \mid x, z)\,P(x)\f$
69:    *  - Public entry points for general identification (ID/IDC):
70:    *      * identifyingIntervention(Y, X)
71:    *      * doCalculus(on, doing)
72:    *      * doCalculusWithObservation(on, doing, knowing)
73:    *
74:    * Returned ASTs are evaluated against the **observational BN** of the bound
75:    * causal model.
76:    */
77:   template < GUM_Numeric GUM_SCALAR >
78:   class DoCalculus {
79:     public:
80:     /// Owned pointer to an AST representing a probability expression.
81:     using FormulaPtr = std::unique_ptr< ASTtree< GUM_SCALAR > >;
82: 
83:     /// Convenience container for name-based overloads.
84:     using NameList = std::vector< std::string >;
85: 
86:     /* ------------------------ Construction ------------------------ */
87: 
88:     explicit DoCalculus(const CausalModel< GUM_SCALAR >& cm) noexcept : _cm{cm} {}
89: 
90:     const CausalModel< GUM_SCALAR >& model() const noexcept;
91: 
92:     /* -------------------- Backdoor / Frontdoor -------------------- */
93: 
94:     FormulaPtr getBackDoorTree(NodeId cause, NodeId effect, const NodeSet& zset) const;
95: 
96:     FormulaPtr getBackDoorTree(std::string_view causeName,
97:                                std::string_view effectName,
98:                                const NameList&  zNames) const;
99: 
100:     FormulaPtr getFrontDoorTree(NodeId cause, NodeId effect, const NodeSet& zset) const;
101: 
102:     FormulaPtr getFrontDoorTree(std::string_view causeName,
103:                                 std::string_view effectName,
104:                                 const NameList&  zNames) const;
105: 
106:     /* --------------------- General identification ----------------- */
107: 
108:     /// ID: identify P(Y | do(X)) (NodeId-based).
109:     FormulaPtr identifyingIntervention(const NodeSet& Y, const NodeSet& X) const;
110: 
111:     /// ID: identify P(Y | do(X)) (name-based).
112:     FormulaPtr identifyingIntervention(const NameList& Y, const NameList& X) const;
113: 
114:     /// Thin wrapper around ID: doCalculus(on, doing)
115:     FormulaPtr doCalculus(const NodeSet& on, const NodeSet& doing) const;
116:     FormulaPtr doCalculus(const NameList& on, const NameList& doing) const;
117: 
118:     /// IDC: identify P(on | do(doing), knowing)
119:     FormulaPtr doCalculusWithObservation(const NodeSet& on,
120:                                          const NodeSet& doing,
121:                                          const NodeSet& knowing) const;
122:     FormulaPtr doCalculusWithObservation(const NameList& on,
123:                                          const NameList& doing,
124:                                          const NameList& knowing) const;
125: 
126:     private:
127:     const CausalModel< GUM_SCALAR >& _cm;
128: 
129:     /* ---------- Helpers for ID/IDC (DAG-only; never mutate CausalModel) ---------- */
130: 
131:     /// c-decomposition (confounding components) among observed nodes.
132:     std::vector< NodeSet > _cDecomposition_(const CausalModel< GUM_SCALAR >& cm) const;
133: 
134:     /// c-decomposition on an induced submodel (observed nodes only).
135:     std::vector< NodeSet > _cDecompositionOn_(const CausalModel< GUM_SCALAR >& sub) const;
136: 
137:     /// Topological order over observed nodes (ignoring latent parents).
138:     std::vector< NodeId > _topoObserved_(const CausalModel< GUM_SCALAR >& cm) const;
139: 
140:     /// Ancestors (in DAG g) of a set T (including T).
141:     static NodeSet _ancestorsIn_(const DAG& g, const NodeSet& T);
142: 
143:     /// DAG copy with all incoming arcs into X removed (G_{\overline X}).
144:     static DAG _removeIncomingInto_(const DAG& dag, const NodeSet& X);
145: 
146:     /// IDC helper: DAG copy with incoming into doing removed AND outgoing from knowing removed.
147:     static DAG _removeInIntoDoing_outOfKnowing_(const DAG&     dag,
148:                                                 const NodeSet& doing,
149:                                                 const NodeSet& knowing);
150: 
151:     /// ID core (recursive), with optional accumulated distribution P (AST) to carry in
152:     /// decompositions.
153:     FormulaPtr _ID_(const CausalModel< GUM_SCALAR >&         cm,
154:                     const NodeSet&                           Y,
155:                     const NodeSet&                           X,
156:                     std::unique_ptr< ASTtree< GUM_SCALAR > > P) const;
157: 
158:     /// Format a hedge exception message.
159:     static std::string _hedgeExceptionMsg(const CausalModel< GUM_SCALAR >& cm,
160:                                           const NodeSet&                   Y,
161:                                           const NodeSet&                   X,
162:                                           const NodeSet&                   V,
163:                                           const NodeSet&                   S);
164:   };
165: 
166: #ifndef GUM_NO_EXTERN_TEMPLATE_CLASS
167:   extern template class DoCalculus< double >;
168: #endif
169: 
170: }   // namespace gum

51:   /**
52:    * @class Counterfactual
53:    * @brief Computes a counterfactual distribution by building a twin model, then
54:    *        evaluating a causal effect on that twin and adapting the result back
55:    *        to the original model’s variables.
56:    *
57:    * High-level workflow:
58:    *  1. Build the **twin** causal model with ::counterFactualModel:
59:    *     - Start from the observational BN.
60:    *     - Identify *idiosyncratic* variables (parentless nodes) and remove any
61:    *       that are in `whatif` or latent.
62:    *     - Run inference on the original BN with the optional `profile` evidence
63:    *       and replace the priors of idiosyncratic variables in the twin by their
64:    *       posteriors from the original BN.
65:    *  2. On the twin model, build a `CausalImpact` for the query
66:    *     P(on | do(whatif), …) and **evaluate** it numerically.
67:    *  3. If `values` is provided, **slice** the numeric tensor using only the
68:    *     assignments present in the result (safe partial instantiation).
69:    *  4. **Adapt** the evaluated tensor back to the original model by rebuilding a
70:    *     tensor with the same variable names (and order) as produced by the twin
71:    *     evaluation, but bound to the original BN’s variables.
72:    *
73:    * Constructors:
74:    *  - Names API:
75:    *      Counterfactual(cm, on, whatif, profile, values)
76:    *    where `on` and `whatif` are sets of variable names; `profile` and `values`
77:    *    are name→label assignments. `profile` is used as observational evidence
78:    *    when computing posteriors for the idiosyncratic roots; `values` gives the
79:    *    specific do-assignments when evaluating the effect and for optional
80:    *    numeric slicing.
81:    *  - IDs API:
82:    *      Counterfactual(cm, onIds, whatifIds, profileIds, valuesIds)
83:    *    same semantics, using node/value identifiers.
84:    *
85:    * Results:
86:    *  - `value()` returns the numeric tensor adapted to the original model’s
87:    *    variables (order mirrors the twin evaluation’s variable sequence).
88:    *  - `getResult()` exposes the symbolic `CausalFormula` produced on the twin
89:    *    model (variable names match those of the original BN).
90:    *
91:    * Notes:
92:    *  - `profile` and `values` can be empty.
93:    *  - `values` is **not** required to build the formula; it is used for the twin
94:    *    evaluation and optional numeric slicing.
95:    *  - Exceptions from evidence insertion, inference, CPT replacement and tensor
96:    *    building may propagate (e.g., unknown variable/label names, inconsistent
97:    *    domains).

139: def causalImpact(cm, *, on, doing, knowing=None, values=None):
140:     """
141:     Identify and evaluate the causal effect of do(doing) on on, optionally
142:     conditioning on knowing.
143: 
144:     The identification procedure tries in order: d-separation (no effect),
145:     backdoor adjustment, frontdoor adjustment, and general do-calculus
146:     (ID algorithm).
147: 
148:     Parameters
149:     ----------
150:     cm : pyagrum.CausalModel
151:         The causal model.
152:     on : str or set of str
153:         Target variable(s) of the causal query. A single string is
154:         automatically converted to a one-element set.
155:     doing : str or set of str
156:         Intervened variable(s) (the do-operator applies to these). A single
157:         string is automatically converted to a one-element set.
158:     knowing : str or set of str, optional
159:         Observed variable(s) to condition on. Default is empty.
160:     values : dict of str → str, optional
161:         Specific values for the on/knowing variables as
162:         ``{variable_name: value_name}``. When provided, the returned tensor
163:         is sliced to those values. Default is no slicing.
164: 
165:     Returns
166:     -------
167:     tuple (pyagrum.CausalImpact, pyagrum.Tensor or None, str)
168:         - The CausalImpact object encoding the identified formula.
169:         - The evaluated tensor P(on | do(doing), knowing), or None if the
170:           effect is not identifiable.
171:         - A string explaining the identification method used or why
172:           identification failed.
173: 
174:     Examples
175:     --------
176:     >>> import pyagrum as gum
177:     >>> bn = gum.BayesNet.fastPrototype('X->Y->Z')
178:     >>> cm = gum.CausalModel(bn)
179:     >>> formula, tensor, expl = gum.causalImpact(cm, on='Z', doing='X')
180:     >>> print(expl)
181:     """
182:     if isinstance(on, str):
183:         on = {on}
184:     if isinstance(doing, str):
185:         doing = {doing}
186:     if isinstance(knowing, str):
187:         knowing = {knowing}
188:     lat, pot, expl = _causalImpact(cm, on, doing,
189:                                    knowing if knowing is not None else set(),
190:                                    values  if values  is not None else {})
191:     pot._model = cm
192:     return lat, (pot if lat.isIdentified() else None), expl

194: def counterfactual(cm, *, on, whatif, profile=None, values=None):
195:     """
196:     Compute a counterfactual distribution using Pearl's twin network method.
197: 
198:     Answers the question: 'Given that we observed *profile*, what would
199:     *on* have been if *whatif* had been set as specified in *values*?'
200: 
201:     The computation follows the three-step algorithm from Pearl (2018),
202:     *The Book of Why*, chapter 8: abduction (update parentless node priors
203:     from the profile), action (apply do(whatif) on the twin model), and
204:     prediction (evaluate the causal effect on the twin).
205: 
206:     Parameters
207:     ----------
208:     cm : pyagrum.CausalModel
209:         The causal model.
210:     on : str or set of str
211:         Target variable(s) of the counterfactual query. A single string is
212:         automatically converted to a one-element set.
213:     whatif : str or set of str
214:         Variable(s) whose values are changed in the counterfactual scenario.
215:         A single string is automatically converted to a one-element set.
216:     profile : dict of str → str, optional
217:         The factual observation as ``{variable_name: value_name}``. This
218:         grounds the counterfactual (step 1: abduction). Default is empty
219:         (no factual observation).
220:     values : dict of str → str, optional
221:         Counterfactual values for the *whatif* variables as
222:         ``{variable_name: value_name}``. If omitted, the full distribution
223:         over all *whatif* values is returned.
224: 
225:     Returns
226:     -------
227:     pyagrum.Tensor
228:         The counterfactual distribution P(on | do(whatif)) evaluated on the
229:         twin model, optionally sliced by *values*.
230: 
231:     Examples
232:     --------
233:     >>> import pyagrum as gum
234:     >>> bn = gum.BayesNet.fastPrototype('X->Y->Z')
235:     >>> cm = gum.CausalModel(bn)
236:     >>> t = gum.counterfactual(cm, on='Z', whatif='X',
237:     ...                        profile={'Y': 'True'}, values={'X': 'False'})
238:     """
